They also afford the most accessible near-future opportunity to study the atmospheres of terrestrial planets.

arxiv-2108-05352.title: High harmonic generation in fullerene molecules
arxiv-2108-05352.creator: H. K. Avetissian, A. G. Ghazaryan, G. F. Mkrtchian
arxiv-2108-05352.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by H. K. Avetissian, A. G. Ghazaryan, G. F. Mkrtchian. Using dynamical Hartree-Fock mean-field theory, we study the high-harmonic generation (HHG) in the fullerene molecules C 60 and C 70 under strong pump wave driving. We consider a strong-field regime and show that the output harmonic radiation exhibits multiple plateaus, whose borders are defined by the molecular excitonic lines and cutoff energies within each plateau scale linearly with the field strength amplitude.

arxiv-2411-05210.title: Algorithmic Autonomy in Data-Driven AI ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06
arxiv-2411-05210.creator: Ge Wang, Roy Pea
arxiv-2411-05210.description: Abstract . In societies increasingly entangled with algorithms, our choices are constantly influenced and shaped by automated systems. This convergence highlights significant concerns for individual autonomy in the age of data-driven AI. It leads to pressing issues such as data-driven segregation, gaps in accountability for algorithmic decisions, and the infringement on essential human rights and values.

arxiv-2411-16441.title: Shortest Path Lengths in Poisson Line Cox Processes: Approximations and Applications
arxiv-2411-16441.creator: Gourab Ghatak Member, IEEE, Sanjoy Kumar Jhawar, Martin Haenggi, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2411-16441.description: Abstract We derive exact expressions for the shortest path length to a point of a Poisson line Cox process (PLCP) from the typical point of the PLCP and from the typical intersection of the underlying Poisson line process (PLP), restricted to a single turn.

arxiv-2501-14324.title: Revealing two orthogonally polarized spectral components in Vela X-1 with IXPE
arxiv-2501-14324.creator: Sofia V. Forsblom, Sergey S. Tsygankov, Valery F. Suleimanov, Alexander A. Mushtukov, Juri Poutanen
arxiv-2501-14324.description: Abstract Polarimetric observations of X-ray pulsars (XRPs) have provided us with the key to unlocking their geometrical properties. Thanks to the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE), the geometries of several XRPs have been determined, providing new insights into their emission mechanisms and magnetic field structures.

arxiv-2506-10419.title: Data-Driven Soil Organic Carbon Sampling: Integrating Spectral Clustering with Conditioned Latin Hypercube Optimization
arxiv-2506-10419.creator: Weiying Zhao, Aleksei Unagaev, Natalia Efremova
arxiv-2506-10419.description: Abstract Soil organic carbon (SOC) monitoring often relies on selecting representative field sampling locations based on environmental covariates. We propose a novel hybrid methodology that integrates spectral clustering—an unsupervised machine learning technique—with conditioned Latin hypercube sampling (cLHS) to enhance the representativeness of SOC sampling.

arxiv-2601-18518.title: Quantum Key Distribution with a Negatively Charged Quantum Dot Single-Photon Source Journal: opticajournal
arxiv-2601-18518.creator: Parvendra Kumar
arxiv-2601-18518.description: Abstract Various quantum key distribution protocols require bright single-photon sources with a very low probability of multiphoton emission. In this work, we investigate single-photon generation from a negatively charged quantum dot embedded in an elliptical pillar microcavity, driven using either resonant excitation or adiabatic rapid passage (ARP).

pmc-10558437.title: COVID-19 pandemic stressors are associated with reported increases in frequency of drunkenness among individuals with a history of alcohol use disorder
pmc-10558437.creator: Jacquelyn L Meyers, Vivia V McCutcheon, Kristina A Horne-Osipenko, Lawrence R Waters, Peter Barr, Grace Chan, David B Chorlian, Emma C Johnson, Sally I-Chun Kuo, John R Kramer, Danielle M Dick, Samuel Kuperman, Chella Kamarajan, Gayathri Pandey, Dzov Singman, Stacey Subbie-Saenz de Viteri, Jessica E
pmc-10558437.description: Some sources report increases in alcohol use have been observed since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly among women. Cross-sectional studies suggest that specific COVID-19-related stressful experiences (e.g., social disconnection) may be driving such increases in the general population. Few studies have explored these topics among individuals with a history of Alcohol Use Disorders (AUD), an especially vulnerable population.

pmc-10615259.title: The Aurora kinase B relocation blocker LXY18 triggers mitotic catastrophe selectively in malignant cells
pmc-10615259.creator: Julia Kalashova, Chenglu Yang, Hongmei Li, Yan Long, Duo Yu, Ting Zhang, Xumei Liu, Namrta Choudhry, Qiong Shi, Thaddeus D. Allen
pmc-10615259.description: The mitotic regulator, Aurora kinase B (AURKB), is frequently overexpressed in malignancy and is a target for therapeutic intervention. The compound, LXY18, is a potent, orally available small molecule that inhibits the proper localization of AURKB during late mitosis, without affecting its kinase activity.

pmc-10616852.title: Machine-Learning-Based Single-Molecule Quantification of Circulating MicroRNA Mixtures
pmc-10616852.creator: Jonathan Jeffet, Sayan Mondal, Amit Federbush, Nadav Tenenboim, Miriam Neaman, Jasline Deek, Yuval Ebenstein, Yohai Bar-Sinai
pmc-10616852.description: MicroRNAs (miRs) are small noncoding RNAs that regulate gene expression and are emerging as powerful indicators of diseases. MiRs are secreted in blood plasma and thus may report on systemic aberrations at an early stage via liquid biopsy analysis. We present a method for multiplexed single-molecule detection and quantification of a selected panel of miRs.

pmc-12559924.title: The Relationship of Prior Concussion and Contact Sport Exposure With Cortical Macro and Microstructure
pmc-12559924.creator: Timothy B Meier, L Tugan Muftuler, Bryna D Goeckner, Nicholas Weyenberg, Daniel L Huber, Lezlie Y España, Anjishnu Banerjee, Andrew R Mayer, Benjamin L Brett
pmc-12559924.description: Changes in cortical gray matter are a key feature of neurodegenerative diseases that have been linked with concussion and repetitive head impacts (RHIs). Prior evidence implicates prior concussion and RHI in reduced cortical thickness or volume in temporal and frontal regions, with results largely restricted to older retired contact sport athletes.

pmc-12824466.title: Bilateral Cytomegalovirus Retinitis With Co-infection of Epstein-Barr Virus and Varicella-Zoster Virus: A Rare Case
pmc-12824466.creator: Hirotaka Kondo, Mariko Egawa, Ryoji Yanai, Yoshinori Mitamura
pmc-12824466.description: Cytomegalovirus retinitis (CMVR) is a form of infectious uveitis, a disease characterized by inflammation of the uvea, the middle layer of the eye. It is caused by the cytomegalovirus (CMV). Although CMVR generally involves a single virus, rare cases have been reported in which multiple viral DNAs have been detected in intraocular fluid using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing.

pmc-13219667.title: Increasing and more consistent use of pre-biopsy MRI in prostate cancer diagnosis: insights from a population-based study in the Netherlands
pmc-13219667.creator: C C Loeff, I G Schoots, P J van Leeuwen, D E Oprea-Lager, S Al-Uwini, L A L M Kiemeney, I M van Oort, K K H Aben, B L Heesterman
pmc-13219667.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveGuidelines recommend MRI before prostate biopsy in men with suspected prostate cancer (PCa). However, real-world data on clinical use are scarce. This study aims to provide comprehensive insight into the nationwide use of pre-biopsy MRI across the Netherlands.Materials and methodsMen with biopsy-proven primary PCa diagnosed between 2019 and 2023, were identified through the Netherlands Cancer Registry (main cohort; n = 50,987). A historical cohort included similar cases from 2015 to 2016 (n = 5183).

pmc-13284056.title: Comparative effects of structured exercise protocols on depression and anxiety symptoms: a network meta-analysis
pmc-13284056.creator: Zhiyuan Zhang, Fengyun Li, Can Han, Wenkun Song, Sifan Pu
pmc-13284056.description: ObjectiveTo systematically compare the intervention effects of eight common structured exercise modalities on depressive and anxiety symptoms in adults using a network meta-analysis approach, providing evidence-based insights for developing precision exercise prescriptions in mental health.MethodsA computer search was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library databases, covering the period from the database establishment to March 31,2026.

pmc-13439201.title: Transcriptomic profiling of HBV transgenic mouse livers reveals ZBP1-associated necroptotic signaling
pmc-13439201.creator: Zean Wang, Mengyuan Zhao, Yun Fu, Lili Liu, Yong Hou, Mei Shi, Fei Gao, Guoliang Zhang
pmc-13439201.description: Although transcriptome studies have been performed in cell culture models of HBV infection, the in vivo hepatic transcriptional response to persistent HBV expression remains incompletely characterized. In addition, whether HBV is associated with activation of necroptotic signaling in the liver has not been fully clarified.

pmc-13455333.title: Effectiveness of THC-containing cannabis for inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review
pmc-13455333.creator: Sebastian Jugl, Silvia Perez-Vilar, Steven Galati, Sukhminder K Sandhu, Hung-Kai Chen, Shao-Hsuan Chang, Yehua Wang, Thorben Kurzbach, Lauren Adkins, Jingchuan Guo, Yan Wang, Almut G Winterstein, Amie Goodin
pmc-13455333.description: BackgroundPatients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) increasingly use cannabis. Studies investigating the effectiveness and safety of cannabis as a therapeutic option for IBD have reported conflicting findings, and recent reviews have not incorporated evidence from real-world studies. This systematic review assessed controlled non-interventional studies and interventional trials evaluating the effectiveness of delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC)-containing cannabis products in patients with IBD.

pmc-13494073.title: Pitfalls in Detecting MET Exon 14 Skipping Variants by DNA- and RNA-Based Next-Generation Sequencing Technologies in a Large Real-World Cohort and Results of the First Multinational External Quality Assessment Schemes
pmc-13494073.creator: Carina Heydt, Michaela A. Ihle, Katharina Ilm, Jan Rehker, Peony Poon, Janna Siemanowski-Hrach, Roberto Pappesch, Svenja Wagener-Ryczek, Christoph Jonas, Jana Fassunke, Richard Riedel, Anne M. Schultheis, Reinhard Buettner, Sabine Merkelbach-Bruse, Udo Siebolts
pmc-13494073.description: MET exon 14 skipping mutations in non–small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) are important biomarkers for targeted therapy, making accurate detection essential. This study analyzed 379 NSCLCs with mutations in MET exon 14 and adjacent splice sites using DNA- and RNA-based next-generation sequencing (NGS).

pmc-13650318.title: Arrhythmic risk in axial spondyloarthritis: a narrative review
pmc-13650318.creator: Dimitrios Bismpos, Jan Wintrich, Christian Ukena, Xenofon Baraliakos, Philipp Sebastian Lange, Philipp Sewerin
pmc-13650318.description: Axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) is a chronic systemic inflammatory disorder affecting the axial skeleton and potentially the peripheral joints as well as extraskeletal tissues. Chronic systemic inflammation is also known to play a major role in the pathogenesis of conduction disturbances and arrhythmias, through chronic fibrotic scarring and cytokine-mediated delay of atrioventricular (AV) conduction as well as atrial remodelling.
